DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: An individual has an appointment with his dentist. He has a choice between travelling to the appointment by car, or leaving the car at home and travelling by bus and then by train. The costs of the journey are given below. $ bus fare 2 train fare 3 car parking charge 4 petrol 2 car wear and tear costs 1 Given this information, what is the opportunity cost to the individual of travelling by car rather than by bus and train?
In the diagram the original production possibility curve is LM. L N consumer goods O P M capital goods What could cause the curve to shift to NP?

options.A: a fall in the working population
options.B: a reallocation of resources from consumer goods to capital goods
options.C: an increase in output per worker
options.D: an increase in unemployment

options.C: the storage of excess production for future sale

questions.questionText: Travellers can cross the English Channel either by the Channel Tunnel or by a sea journey. The table gives details of the passengers, in thousands, using these services between 2005 and 2015. Between 2005 and 2015 the price of the Channel Tunnel fell and the price of sea journeys rose. Channel Tunnel sea journey year passengers passengers 2005 17005 23693 2010 18303 21883 2015 20864 21000 What does the data suggest?

options.A: The cross elasticity of demand between the two services is positive.
options.B: The market for crossing the English Channel grew continuously over the period.
options.C: The rate of decline in sea journeys accelerated over the period.
options.D: The two services for crossing the English Channel are complementary.

If the advice were accepted, how might the effect be illustrated on demand and supply diagrams for fizzy drinks and for sugar? diagram for fizzy drinks diagram for sugar

options.A: demand curve moves to the left movement up the supply curve
options.B: demand curve moves to the left movement down the supply curve

questions.questionText: Singapore imports almost all of its raw materials and its exports are a high percentage of its GDP. The price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports are each less than 1. What would be the likely impact of a depreciation of the Singapore dollar?

options.A: The domestic inflation rate would fall.
options.B: The government’s budget deficit would move to surplus.
options.C: The price of imports would fall.
options.D: The value of exports would fall.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of a tariff on a product. price domestic supply P world supply plus tariff P world supply domestic demand O quantity From this diagram, what determines the gain the tariff generates for domestic producers?

options.D: the tariff rate and the price elasticity of domestic supply

questions.questionText: The European Union consists of a group of countries with free trade between its members and a common external tariff on trade with non-members. What would weaken the operation of this customs union?

options.B: differences in wage costs between members
options.C: entry tests for seasonal migrant workers
options.D: one member country agreeing a trade deal with a non-member country

questions.questionText: Which change is most likely to result in a worsening of a country’s balance of payments?

options.A: a reduction in remittances from citizens who work abroad
options.B: a rise in domestic rates of direct taxation
options.C: an expansion in the economy of a major trading partner
options.D: an increase in domestic interest rates

questions.questionText: What must be true if an economy is experiencing inflation?

options.B: Aggregate supply is decreasing.
options.C: The interest rate is increasing.
options.D: The real value of money is decreasing.

questions.questionText: What is the most likely consequence of an appreciation in the value of the Malaysian ringgit?

options.B: a fall in the rate of growth of the general price level in Malaysia
options.C: a reduction in the volume of imports into Malaysia
options.D: an improvement in the Malaysian balance of trade in services
